summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update20.json → valid=true). Sharpened the snapshot-install coverage record by reading what its convergence assertion actually compares. The helper compares, across all nodes, the ordered slice of command payloads each FSM applied and the sequence of configurations each FSM recorded, retrying until a longstop deadline before failing on a length or content mismatch (testing.go:614-677), and the FSM it inspects holds exactly those applied payloads, replaced wholesale on Restore (testing.go:76-107); it reads no Raft log, applied/commit index, replication cursor or node configuration. Two consequences recorded as a new Fact plus a successor interpretation for the same question (earlier interpretation and counterevidence preserved): the assertion is genuinely sensitive to a follower that stops making progress — a node stuck in the snapshot loop would stop applying the leader's later commands, so payload lengths would diverge and the test would fail once the retry window expired — so the retained suite is not vacuous about stalls of this shape; but it is blind to the state the recorded cycle concerns, so a follower whose applied payloads match while its log and cursor state do not would pass. Since no retained scenario constructs the cycle's premise (unit tests cover only the index-behind case; the randomized harness effectively disables snapshots, both recorded earlier), that sensitivity was never aimed at it — the honest summary being that the retained evidence would likely catch a stalled follower if a test set the premise up, and that none does. Counterevidence kept explicit, including that some other harness helpers do compare node configurations, and that the sensitivity claim assumes the retry window is long enough for the stall to be observed (not measured).
